name: Command-Line History via Process-Creation Auditing (4688 / Sysmon EID 1)
os_min: N/A - Event ID 4688 command-line logging requires Windows Vista/Server 2008 or later plus the specific audit policy below enabled; Sysmon requires separate installation on any supported Windows version.
location: Security.evtx (Event ID 4688, Process Command Line field) and/or Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon%4Operational.evtx (Event ID 1, CommandLine field).
purpose: This entry documents the mechanism that must be in place for command-line arguments to be captured at process-creation time at all - it is not the general Security or Sysmon event log entry, but specifically what has to be configured (or not) for the Process Command Line / CommandLine field to be populated, and how analysts use that field to reconstruct exactly what an attacker typed or a script executed.
key_fields: 4688 requires two separate settings to show a command line: (1) Audit Process Creation itself, under Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Advanced Audit Policy Configuration > Detailed Tracking - without this, no 4688 events are generated at all; (2) the separate policy 'Include command line in process creation events', under Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > System > Audit Process Creation - without this second setting, 4688 events fire but the Process Command Line field is blank

Registry equivalent of the second setting: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\Audit\ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled (DWORD 1 = enabled); both settings default to Not Configured / disabled out of the box
4688 Process Command Line - the full command line of the newly created process, logged in plain text once both policies above are enabled
4688 New Process Name / Creator Process Name - full image paths of the child and parent processes, correlating via Process ID and Logon ID

Sysmon Event ID 1 (Process Create) CommandLine and ParentCommandLine fields - captured by default as part of the event schema the moment Sysmon is installed and its configuration does not explicitly filter out Event ID 1; unlike 4688, there is no separate 'include command line' toggle to enable - if Sysmon logs a Process Create event at all, the full command line is in it

Sysmon Event ID 1 also carries ProcessGuid, Hashes (SHA1 by default, or MD5/SHA256/IMPHASH depending on config), and integrity level alongside the command line, giving more built-in context than 4688 for the same event
normal_baseline: On a host where both 4688 audit settings are enabled, or where Sysmon is deployed with a config that does not suppress Event ID 1, process-creation events accumulate continuously with plausible command lines matching normal software behavior (installers, browser helper processes, scheduled maintenance scripts) and legible arguments; on a host where only 'Audit Process Creation' is enabled without the command-line addendum, 4688 events exist but every Process Command Line field is empty - a very common and easily overlooked misconfiguration that silently blinds command-line reconstruction while giving the false impression that process auditing is fully enabled.
anomalies: 4688 events present but every Process Command Line field is blank across the board - indicates the 'Include command line in process creation events' policy was never enabled, meaning command-line reconstruction from this host is not possible from 4688 alone regardless of the time period examined
A command line containing encoded/obfuscated content (e.g. powershell.exe -EncodedCommand, base64 blobs, excessive character escaping) used specifically to defeat casual review of the logged text
A command line invoking a living-off-the-land binary (certutil, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32, bitsadmin) with arguments inconsistent with that binary's normal administrative use

A gap in 4688 or Sysmon Event ID 1 volume that does not align with any other logged activity stopping - Sysmon or the audit policy may have been reconfigured/tampered with rather than the host simply going idle

Sysmon Event ID 1 present with populated CommandLine while the Security log's 4688 events for the same time window show blank Process Command Line fields - confirms the audit-policy gap above and that Sysmon is the only reliable source of command-line data on that host

A parent-child command-line pair showing a script interpreter (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe) spawned from an Office application, browser, or PDF reader with an unexpected command line - the standard initial-access-to-execution pivot point analysts search for first
anti_forensic_notes: An attacker who disables or stops the EventLog service, clears the Security log (which itself generates a 4688-independent 1102 event), or reconfigures/uninstalls Sysmon removes future command-line visibility going forward, but cannot retroactively populate command lines that were never captured because the audit policy addendum was off in the first place - the absence of command-line data on a host is therefore ambiguous between 'never configured' and 'deliberately tampered with' and must be checked against the actual policy/registry state and against whether other event types from the same source continued logging normally.
